_doc: Revert-verify for the eslint-debt ratchet (issue #4497). The issue reported that the required `lint` job pointed eslint at ONE of six TypeScript packages; the load-bearing half it did not name is that the step carried `continue-on-error: true` (fa5251f8, "allow lint WARNINGS to not fail CI"), so the job was green at ANY number of eslint ERRORS — measured on main@204898e1: `npm run lint` rc=1 with 56 errors, `lint` green. This change removes the flagged step and replaces it with the guard. Axes EL1-EL11 live in check-eslint-debt.test.ts; the subject is the guard script itself. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this spec> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout. Recorded runs: see the PR body.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/scripts/check-eslint-debt.mjs
_note_broad_mutant: M1 is the mutant the issue's acceptance criteria name verbatim ("narrow the scope back to one package"). It is BROAD by construction — narrowing the sweep starves every axis whose fixture puts its finding in the second package — so its `expect` list is taken from the recorded run, not from the mutant's theme (integration-test-revert-verify §A44/§A54). M2-M11 are the single-concern mutants: each names one guarantee and reddens the one axis that holds it.

M1_scope_narrowed_to_one_package._why: The mutant #4497 asks for: the sweep collapses to a single package, which is the pre-fix state of the root `lint` script. Broad on purpose — see _note_broad_mutant.
M1_scope_narrowed_to_one_package.to:
const { inScope: _derived, notLintable } = derivePackages();
const inScope = _derived.slice(0, 1);

M2_ts_project_exclusion_ignored._why: Drops the second conjunct of scope derivation, so a package eslint CANNOT judge (packages/cli in production, `excluded` in the fixture) is swept anyway and its fatals/findings reach the verdict. EL4 holds the property that such a package is dropped WITH its reason printed.

M3_fatals_absorbed_silently._why: A fatal parse error inside the derived scope stops being rc=2. Without this guard the run would call itself clean over files it never judged — the exact shape that 122 baselined `cli` parse errors would have had.

M4_counts_not_compared._why: The baseline stores per-pair counts; if nothing reads them, a SECOND instance of an already-baselined pair is absorbed silently. This is the hole check-cli-types.mjs had to close once it noticed its own `count` field was never read.

M5_gone_pairs_not_reported._why: Removes the second direction of fail-loud: a baselined pair that no longer occurs stops being a finding, so the baseline silently stops describing the code and becomes licence rather than a ratchet.

M6_warnings_gated_as_errors._why: Re-breaks what fa5251f8 actually asked for: warnings would fail the job. EL8 is the axis that keeps the author's recorded intent true while the mechanism changed under it.

M7_zero_linted_files_reads_green._why: Removes the population floor. An in-scope package whose src/ exists but yields no judged file would read as clean — paths visited reported as content judged (self-satisfying-metric-weak-verifier §A58).

M8_unreadable_baseline_reads_green._why: An unparseable baseline falls back to an empty one, so every run would exit 0 over a baseline nobody can read — the disarm that check-cli-types.mjs documents for its own `--update`.
M8_unreadable_baseline_reads_green.to: baseline = (() => { try { return JSON.parse(readFileSync(BASELINE, "utf8")); } catch { return { scope: inScope, entries: [] }; } })();

M9_narrowed_sweep_reads_green._why: The sweep may cover fewer packages than the baseline names without saying so — i.e. the run judges less than it claims and still passes. This is the quiet half of the #4497 defect.

M10_new_pairs_not_reported._why: The ratchet stops reporting NEW (file, rule) pairs — a measurer with no consequence, which is precisely what widening the path list under a live `continue-on-error` would have shipped.

M11_report_mode_gates._why: `--report` is the advisory reading and must never gate; if it falls through to the verdict, `npm run lint:report` starts failing an author's working tree on pre-existing debt.
